newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lamfalussy-EMI still mulling minimum reserves.
newsitem.headline: Lamfalussy-EMI still mulling minimum reserves.

text.p: European Monetary Institute (EMI) President Alexandre Lamfalussy said on Wednesday the EMI was still considering whether to introduce the minimum reserve requirement as a policy instrument, as suggested by the Bundesbank.

Referring to the issue of introducing minimum reserves, Lamfalussy said the EMI's Council had decided to work out the technical foundations for such a step and to reach a decision next year on how to proceed, according to a summary of a speech he was due to hold at Karlsruhe University.
Lamfalussy said securities repurchase agreements would be a leading monetary policy instrument for the future European central bank. The EMI is the forerunner of the planned European central bank.
The EMI also plans to introduce policy instruments which make it possible to establish a ceiling and a floor for money market instruments, Lamfalussy said, according to the summary.

It was considering introducing a deposit facility enabling banks to deposit excess liquidity at the end of the day, and a special refinancing line enabling banks to plug liquidity deficits at the end of the day.
The EMI was also considering enabling smaller banks to have direct access to central bank money through open market operations with a duration of, for example, three months, Lamfalussy said.
The summary was made available by the EMI in Frankfurt.
